# Land changes without a queue

## Intent

Landing adds a change's commits to its target branch, and many agents land on one repository at the same time. Parley lands optimistically: `parleyd` rebases the change onto the current head of the target on the server and moves the target with a compare-and-swap, with no queue and no per-workspace lock, so that changes touching different things land side by side, a moved target only causes another try, and only a real conflict stops a land and comes back as data. Every land is recorded as a durable land attempt whose bookkeeping is atomic, so a land is either fully recorded or did not happen, also across a restart.

## Goals

- One call, `POST /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/land`, lands a change or its whole stack and answers `200` (landed), `202` (still running), `409` (precondition, policy block or conflict) or `503` (failed).
- Two lands on the same target that do not conflict both end `landed`, in either order, without either caller retrying (LAND-US-01).
- A conflicting land leaves the target where it was and returns a conflict report naming the files and the landed changes collided with (LAND-US-02).
- The ref move, the change's transition to `landed`, the commit mapping, the attempt's final status and the `parley.change.land` event are one atomic step; after a crash the hub is not landed, or landed with all of them (LAND-FR-015, LAND-US-11).
- An attempt that was `running` when the hub stopped ends in a final status after the next start (LAND-FR-019).
- Land attempts are readable per change, per workspace and by id, and the CLI offers `parley change land`, `parley change lands`, `parley land list` and `parley land show`.

## Requirements

### Who may land (LAND-FR-001, LAND-FR-003, PLAT-FR-062)

`POST /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/land` names the target workspace. A PAT needs `changes:write`. The route's need is `read` plus one condition: the caller has write access to the target workspace (owner, or the admin token), or the caller's user is the change's author (the user behind the credential that opened the change) while the workspace setting `land.by_author` is true (default). An org member who is not the author, or who is the author while `land.by_author` is false, gets `403 forbidden`. A caller with no read access gets `404 not_found`. An unknown change number is `404 change_not_found`. An archived target workspace is `409 workspace_archived`.

A token bound to a fork F reaches, on F's parent, the land route and `GET …/changes/:number/lands` only for a change whose source workspace is F, and `GET …/lands/:id` only for an attempt that lands such a change; with `stack: true` every change the attempt would cover must have source F. Otherwise the answer is `403 token_bound`, as it is for `GET …/lands` on the parent.

The body is `{"expected_version"?: int, "stack"?: bool, "override"?: {"reason": string}, "session_id"?: string}`; the query `wait` is whole seconds, 0 to 60, default 30. A wrong type, an `expected_version` below 1, an `override` without a non-empty `reason`, or a `wait` outside 0 to 60 is `400 invalid_request`. A `session_id` that fails the session-linking rule of §14 is `400 unknown_session`. None of these creates a land attempt. The route is a create route for `Idempotency-Key` (PLAT-FR-015).

### Preconditions (LAND-FR-010)

Checked in this order, the first failure deciding; none creates an attempt:

1. the change is `open`, else `409 change_not_open`;
2. `expected_version`, when given, equals the current version, else `409 version_mismatch`;
3. no other land attempt covering this change is `running`, else `409 land_in_progress` with that attempt in `details`;
4. every change below it in the stack is landed, unless `stack` is true, else `409 depends_on_unlanded`.

Of two simultaneous land calls for one change, exactly one creates an attempt; the other gets `409 land_in_progress`. After the first finished `landed`, a further call gets `409 change_not_open`.

### The land attempt (§8.3.2)

A land that passes the preconditions creates a durable attempt before anything else happens: `id` (UUID), `workspace_slug`, `target_branch`, `changes` (numbers, bottom first), `status` (`running`, then one of the final `landed`, `conflict`, `blocked`, `failed`), `trigger` (`manual`; `auto_land` when package 29 starts it), `strategy` (`rebase` or `squash`, read once from `land.strategy`), `attempts`, `onto_sha`, `landed_sha`, `noop`, `commits` (`{change, version_sha, landed_sha}`), `conflict`, `blocked` (`{change, status, requirements[]}`), `error` (`contention`, `timeout`, `origin_rejected`, `internal`), `override`, `policy_revision`, `requested_by` (`{actor_type, actor_id, username}`), `session_id`, `created_at`, `finished_at`. A final attempt never changes. The attempt lands the version each change had when the attempt was created; a version that arrives later is not landed by it.

### Policy gate (LAND-FR-011)

For each change of the attempt, bottom first, the gate is asked once with the workspace, the change, its version, the caller and the `override` of the request. It answers a status (`ready`, `pending`, `blocked`), an optional reason, the requirements, the policy revision and whether an override was applied. The gate is a registration point: package 27 registers its evaluator; with none registered the default answers `ready`, revision 0. The override rule is a second registration point, which package 29 registers: for a request that carries `override` and a gate answer that is not `ready`, it says whether the override lets that answer pass; with no rule registered no override is ever applied. A passed answer counts as `ready`. When any answer is not `ready` the attempt ends `blocked` with `blocked` naming the first such change; the target is untouched, the change stays `open`, and the HTTP answer is `409 policy_blocked` with the attempt in `details`. The attempt records the revision the gate reported and `override: {reason}` only when the override rule let at least one change pass. The gate is not asked again when the compare-and-swap is retried, so a policy change or a withdrawn approval during a land does not affect it (§8.10).

### Replay (LAND-FR-012, LAND-FR-013)

Read the target head *T*. The change's own commits are the commits of its version that are not in its base.

- `rebase`: each commit is replayed in order; author, author date and message are kept; the committer is `[land].committer_name` and `[land].committer_email`. When the version already sits directly on *T* the commits are used as they are.
- `squash`: one commit per change, with the tree of the replayed head. Message: the change title, a blank line, the intent, a blank line, the trailers `Parley-Change: <slug>#<number>`, `Parley-Session: <id>` when the change has a session, and one `Co-authored-by: Name <email>` per other distinct author of the change's commits. Author: the author of the version's head commit.
- A commit whose content is already in *T* is dropped. If nothing is left the attempt ends `landed` with `noop: true`, `landed_sha` = *T*, `commits` empty; the target does not move and the change becomes `landed` with `landed.sha` = *T*.
- If a commit does not apply the attempt ends `conflict` with a conflict report: `target_sha`, `head_sha`, `base_sha`, `commit_sha`, `files` (`path`, `kind`, `base`, `ours`, `theirs`, `landed_by`), `landed_changes` (`{number, title, landed_sha, session_id}` of the changes landed between `base_sha` and `target_sha` that touched a conflicted file) and `change`. The target is untouched, the change stays `open` and reads `mergeable: conflict` with that report, and the HTTP answer is `409 land_conflict` with the attempt in `details`.

### Compare-and-swap and the atomic step (LAND-FR-014, LAND-FR-015, LAND-FR-021)

The target moves from *T* to the new head only if it still is *T*. If it moved (another land, a sync, a direct push), the replay starts again on the new head and `attempts` grows by one. After `[land].max_attempts` tries (default 10) the attempt ends `failed` with `error: "contention"`. A target branch that no longer exists ends the attempt `failed` with `error: "internal"`.

The ref move, each change's transition to `landed` with its `landed` object, the mapping of each landed commit to its change, the attempt's final status and one `parley.change.land` event per landed change are one atomic step. The move also produces `parley.git.push` for the target ref with `via: "land"` and `direct: false`. Landing moves protected and unprotected targets alike; the push rules do not apply to it.

Attempts for different changes run concurrently, also on one target; nothing but the compare-and-swap excludes them. They run on a pool of `[land].workers` workers (default 8) that bounds how many replays are computed at once and never orders them; an attempt waiting for a worker is `running`.

### Stack landing (LAND-FR-016)

With `stack: true` the attempt covers the change and every unlanded change below it; a change below that is already landed is skipped. Preconditions 1 and 3 hold for every covered change. All are replayed bottom first onto *T* (with `squash`, one commit per change, in order) and the target moves once, to the top. One conflict or one gate miss ends the whole attempt with nothing landed, and `conflict.change` or `blocked.change` names the change.

### After landing (LAND-FR-017, LAND-FR-018)

After the atomic step, each best effort and never changing the attempt or the answer: delete the source branch when `land.delete_source` is true, its head still is the landed version's head (compare-and-swap) and no other `draft` or `open` change uses it; schedule mergeability checks for the other `draft` and `open` changes on the target; call the registered after-landing hooks (restack of dependants, fork early expiry, carry-patch rebuild). Nothing is pushed to origin or a forge. A registered target guard may, before the target moves, end the attempt `blocked` with its reason or `failed` with `error: "origin_rejected"`; a guard that cannot decide returns an error, and the attempt ends `failed` with `error: "internal"`. In none of the three cases does the target move. A registered request guard is asked in the land route before the preconditions and may refuse the request with its own status and `error_type`; no attempt is created then (package 29 registers its path-limit check and its override refusal this way). Each after-landing hook receives the landed attempt with the target workspace, the update of the target branch (`ref`, `before`, `after`), the attempt's session id (or none) and, for every landed change, its number, its source workspace and branch, and its landed commit.

### Durability, time and the answer (LAND-FR-019, LAND-FR-020)

An attempt that was `running` when the hub stopped is run again from the preconditions at the next start. One attempt is bounded by `[land].timeout` (default 5 min) and then ends `failed` with `error: "timeout"`. The land call waits up to `wait` seconds: `200` with the attempt when `landed`; `409 land_conflict` or `409 policy_blocked`; `503 land_failed` with the attempt in `details`; `202` with the attempt while it is still `running`. Every attempt ending `conflict`, `blocked` or `failed` emits `parley.change.land_fail` (`land_id`, `status`, `reason`, `files`).

`[land]` keys: `max_attempts` (int, 10), `timeout` (duration, `5m`), `workers` (int, 8), `committer_name` (`Parley`), `committer_email` (`parley@localhost`).

### Reading land attempts (§8.5)

`GET …/changes/:number/lands` lists a change's attempts; `GET …/lands` lists the workspace's, filtered by `status` (repeatable), `target_branch` and `since`, paged with `limit` and `cursor`; both newest first. `GET …/lands/:id` reads one, or `404 land_not_found`. All need `changes:read` and read access. Attempts are kept for the life of the workspace.

### CLI (§8.6)

`parley change land <slug> <number>` with `--stack`, `--expected-version <n>`, `--override <reason>`, `--session <id>`, `--wait`, `--timeout`, `--poll-interval` calls the land route and, with `--wait`, polls `GET …/lands/:id`. It prints the attempt; a conflict or block prints the envelope. Exit 0 when `landed`, 1 for any other final status or a timeout, 2 for usage. `parley change lands <slug> <number>`, `parley land list <slug>` (`--status` repeatable, `--target`, `--since`, `--limit`, `--cursor`) and `parley land show <slug> <land-id>` print the routes' answers.

### End-to-end flows

1. An agent runs `parley change land` on an open change; `parleyd` creates the attempt, replays, moves the target and records everything in one step; a git client fetching the target sees the commits.
2. Two agents land non-conflicting changes on one target at the same moment; both attempts end `landed` and the target holds both.
3. An agent lands a change that conflicts with a change landed meanwhile; the answer is `409 land_conflict` with the report, and the target has not moved.
4. An operator stops `parleyd` while an attempt is `running` and starts it again; the attempt ends `landed`.

## Design Decisions

1. **Language Go, git as a subprocess (2.38 or later), SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite`, `net/http`, `cobra`**: the project-wide decisions; replay uses `git merge-tree --write-tree` and `git commit-tree`, which need no working tree.
2. **The atomic step is a journal entry, the ref compare-and-swap, then one store transaction.** The journal entry (attempt, ref, *T*, new head, commits) is committed first. At start, before requests are served, an entry whose ref holds the new head gets its bookkeeping completed; any other entry is dropped and the attempt runs again. A git ref and a store row cannot share a transaction, and this gives the two states LAND-FR-015 demands.
3. **The policy gate interface lives in `internal/land`**, so this package does not import `internal/policy`; package 27 `landing_policy`, which depends on this package, registers its evaluator as the gate. With no gate registered every change is `ready` (decision 3 of §17.3).
4. **`override` is validated for shape only; the rule is package 29's (LAND-FR-002).** `internal/land` declares an override rule (does this override let this gate answer pass) and request guards (asked before the preconditions; a refusal is returned as given). Package 29 registers the rule, a request guard that refuses an override the caller may not use, and a request guard for path limits. With nothing registered an override is accepted, never applied, and the attempt records `override: null`.
5. **Preconditions run in the request, before an attempt exists.** So `change_not_open`, `version_mismatch` and `depends_on_unlanded` carry no `details`; `land_in_progress` carries the running attempt. The PRD says "with the land attempt in `details` where one was created".
6. **A re-run after a restart whose change is no longer landable** (not `open`, target missing) ends `failed` with `error: "internal"`: the error enumeration has no closer value.
7. **`[land].timeout` counts from the attempt's creation**, and from the re-queue after a restart; waiting for a worker is inside it.
8. **`reason` of `parley.change.land_fail`**: `conflict` for a conflict; the gate's or guard's reason for a block, `policy` when it gives none; the `error` value for a failure. The PRD lists the member without values.
9. **`parley change land` without `--wait` exits 0 on a `202`** and prints the running attempt: the hub answered success and no final status exists yet.
10. **The CLI's land request times out after 70 seconds** instead of 30, because the hub may hold the call for up to 60.
11. **A fork-bound token asking for a change or attempt that is not its fork's gets `403 token_bound`**; an unknown number or id still gets its `404`.
12. **Invalid `[land]` values stop the start**: `max_attempts` and `workers` below 1, a `timeout` that is not positive, an empty committer name or email.
13. **Hooks, guards and observers are registration points of `internal/land`**, so packages 16, 24, 29, 37 and 51 attach without this package depending on them. A final observer receives the final attempt (trigger, changes, status, `attempts`, `created_at`, `finished_at`); package 51 derives its metrics from it and package 29 the outcome of an `auto_land` attempt.
14. **The session-linking rule is asked through a session interface of `internal/land`** with two operations, check and record, which package 49 `agent_sessions_and_usage` installs from the linking check and the recording operation that `internal/session` exports. An attempt with a session records one `land` link in the transaction that creates it. Until an implementation is installed, every `session_id` is refused with `unknown_session`: accepting an unchecked reference would attribute work to a session nobody verified.
15. **One conflict report type.** A failed replay is reported in `ConflictReport`, the type package 20 declares in `internal/gitrepo/conflictreport.go` and packages 21, 23 and 24 already use; the kind and the three sides of each file come from the replay of `internal/gitrepo`. This package adds, in `internal/land/conflict.go`, the attribution that fills `landed_changes` and each `landed_by` from the landed-commit mapping, and sets `change` in a stack land. Package 26 reuses that attribution for the other producers.
16. **The target moves through the ref writer of package 18** (`pushrule.Apply` in `internal/gitserver/pushrule`, `via: "land"`) with an allowed verdict for the one update that this package builds itself, without calling `Evaluate`, because the push rules do not apply to a land.
17. **A target guard answers one of three things or returns an error (with package 37).** The answers are allow, refuse with a reason (`blocked`) and origin rejected with a message (`failed`, `origin_rejected`); an error, which package 37's guard returns when it cannot decide, ends the attempt `failed` with `error: "internal"`. A guard error never allows. The after-landing hook carries the target workspace, the branch update (`ref`, `before`, `after`) and the session id because package 37's rebuild trigger and mirror need them.
18. **Branch globs are package 11's.** The one matcher is `internal/workspace/branchglob.go` of package 11; package 18 calls it and has none of its own, and this package matches no glob.
19. **Composition is in `internal/hub/land.go`**, as package 03 lays down: the routes, the pool and recovery are registered there and nowhere else. This package registers no after-landing hook itself. Packages built earlier than this one (16, 24) add their registration line to `internal/hub/land.go` when this package exists, and packages built later (29, 37) register from their own `internal/hub/<area>.go`.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task.
- **Protected branch**: A branch that moves only by landing a change, by sync from origin, or by a direct fast-forward push from the workspace's owner or the admin token. Nobody can force-push or delete it. By default the default branch.
- **Change**: The unit of work: a proposal to add the commits of a source branch to a target branch, with a number, a title, an intent, versions and a state.
- **Version**: One head of a change's source branch.
- **Stack**: Changes linked by `depends_on`, lowest first.
- **Landing**: Adding a change's commits to its target branch: a server-side rebase followed by a compare-and-swap of the target ref.
- **Land attempt**: One request to land a change (or a stack), with its outcome.
- **Conflict report**: The structured description of why a rebase could not be done: files, kinds, and the landed changes involved.
- **Policy**: A workspace's ordered rules that map touched paths to landing requirements.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it). A token bound to a fork also reaches its own changes, and the awareness and policy reads, on the fork's parent.
- **Session**: An agent session: who ran, on which workspace, with what token usage, and which changes it produced.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Who may land and what a land request may carry

**Rationale:** Landing writes to the target branch, yet an org member must be able to land their own change from a fork; the entry checks decide this before any attempt exists (LAND-FR-001, LAND-FR-003).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] IF a PAT without `changes:write` calls the land route, or a PAT without `changes:read` calls one of the three land read routes, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request before looking up the workspace or the change
   → HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`, the same for an existing and an unknown workspace; no land attempt is created
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub test fixture: a real store in t.TempDir(), a bare repository created with git init whose branch main holds one commit, a ready workspace `api` owned by user `owner`, and the land routes mounted on the real server pipeline with stub authentication
   ```
   in internal/land/routes_test.go, a table over {POST …/changes/1/land with a PAT holding only changes:read, GET …/changes/1/lands, GET …/lands and GET …/lands/<id> with a PAT holding only git:read}, each against the existing workspace `api` and against the unknown slug `nope`: assert status == 403 and error_type == 'insufficient_scope' in both cases; assert count(land attempts) == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN an authenticated caller with the scope `changes:write` (or a credential without scopes) calls `POST /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/land`, THE parleyd SHALL admit the caller when the caller has write access to the target workspace, or when the caller's user is the author of the change and the workspace setting `land.by_author` is true, and refuse every other caller
   → owner, admin token and the authoring member under `land.by_author: true` proceed to the preconditions; a member who is not the author, or the author under `land.by_author: false`, gets HTTP 403 `forbidden`; a caller with no read access gets HTTP 404 `not_found`; a refused call creates no land attempt
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub test fixture: a real store in t.TempDir(), a bare repository created with git init whose branch main holds one commit, a ready workspace `api` owned by user `owner`, and the land routes mounted on the real server pipeline with stub authentication
   - setup: users `member-a` and `member-b` are members of the workspace's organization; `member-a` owns a fork of `api` and authored the change
   ```
   in internal/land/routes_test.go, a table over callers of POST …/changes/N/land for an open change authored by `member-a` from her fork: {owner API key -> 200, admin token -> 200, member-a with land.by_author true -> 200, member-a with land.by_author false -> 403 forbidden, member-b (not the author) -> 403 forbidden, a user with no access -> 404 not_found with the same body as for slug `nope`}; for each refused row assert count(land attempts) == 0 and the target head is unchanged; for each 200 row assert body.status == 'landed'
   ```

### REQ-2: Preconditions and the land attempt record

**Rationale:** A caller must learn at once why a land cannot start, and every land that does start must leave a durable record a caller can poll (LAND-FR-010, §8.3.2).

   Check: integration

   ```

### REQ-3: The policy gate

**Rationale:** Nothing lands past policy, but policy is another package's; landing asks one gate once per change and obeys its answer (LAND-FR-011).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a worker starts a `running` land attempt, THE parleyd SHALL ask the registered policy gate exactly once for each change of the attempt, bottom first, passing the workspace, the change, the version being landed and the caller; for an answer that is not `ready` on a request that carries `override`, ask the registered override rule whether the override lets that answer pass; proceed to the replay only when every answer is `ready` or passed
   → with no gate registered the default gate answers `ready` with policy revision 0; with no override rule registered no override is applied; the attempt records the `policy_revision` the gate reported; neither the gate nor the rule is asked again when the compare-and-swap is retried
   Check: unit
   - setup: an engine fixture: a real store and a bare repository in t.TempDir(), a workspace `api` with branch main, the default gate, and a helper that opens a change from a branch with given commits
   ```
   in internal/land/gate_test.go with a recording gate: run an attempt for one change with override {reason: 'r'} while a second writer moves main once so that the compare-and-swap is retried: assert gate.calls == 1 and the call carried slug 'api', the change number, its current version and the caller; a recording override rule registered beside it was not asked, because the gate answered ready; assert the attempt ended landed with attempts == 2 and policy_revision == the revision the gate returned (7); then with no gate and no override rule registered run an attempt: assert it ended landed with policy_revision == 0 and override == null even though the request carried an override; then with a gate that answers pending and no override rule: assert the attempt ended blocked although the request carried an override
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF the gate answers `pending` or `blocked` for a change of the attempt, THEN THE parleyd SHALL end the attempt `blocked` without replaying or moving anything
   → the attempt is final with `status` `blocked` and `blocked` = `{change, status, requirements[]}` of the first change, bottom first, that was not `ready`; the HTTP answer is 409 with `error_type` `policy_blocked` and the land attempt in `error.details`; the target does not move and the change stays `open`; one `parley.change.land_fail` event is written
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub test fixture: a real store in t.TempDir(), a bare repository created with git init whose branch main holds one commit, a ready workspace `api` owned by user `owner`, and the land routes mounted on the real server pipeline with stub authentication
   ```
   in internal/land/routes_test.go with a gate stub, a table over gate answers {pending with one unsatisfied requirement, blocked with reason 'merge_commits'}: r = land(change); assert r.status == 409 and r.error_type == 'policy_blocked'; d = r.error.details; assert d.status == 'blocked' and d.blocked.change == number and d.blocked.status == the gate's status and d.blocked.requirements == the gate's requirements and d.finished_at != null and d.landed_sha == null; assert the target head is unchanged and the change reads state open; assert one parley.change.land_fail event with metadata.land_id == d.id, status 'blocked' and reason 'policy' for the pending row and 'merge_commits' for the other; assert no parley.change.land event
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN the registered override rule lets the request's override pass the gate answer of at least one change of the attempt, THE parleyd SHALL record `override` on the attempt as `{reason}` with the reason of the request
   → the final land attempt and the `parley.change.land` event metadata carry `override` = `{reason}`; when every change was `ready` without the rule, or the rule passed none, both carry null
   Check: unit
   - setup: an engine fixture: a real store and a bare repository in t.TempDir(), a workspace `api` with branch main, the default gate, and a helper that opens a change from a branch with given commits

   in internal/land/gate_test.go with a gate stub that answers pending and an override rule stub that lets pending pass: run an attempt whose request has override {reason: 'hotfix'}; assert the rule was asked once with the gate's answer; assert the final attempt is landed with override == {reason: 'hotfix'}; assert the parley.change.land event's metadata.override == {reason: 'hotfix'}; with a gate that answers ready and the same rule assert the rule is not asked and both are null; with a gate that answers blocked and a rule that lets only pending pass assert the attempt ends blocked with override null
   ```

### REQ-4: Replay of the change onto the target head

**Rationale:** The server does the rebase so that no client needs a clone, and a commit that does not apply must come back as data, not as a half-moved branch (LAND-FR-012, LAND-FR-013).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN an attempt with strategy `rebase` replays a change whose version does not sit directly on the target head, THE parleyd SHALL replay each of the change's own commits in order onto the target head, keeping each commit's author, author date and message and setting the committer to the landing identity of `[land].committer_name` and `[land].committer_email`
   → the new target history is the target head followed by one new commit per own commit, in order; `commits` holds one `{change, version_sha, landed_sha}` per landed commit and `landed_sha` is the last one; the default committer is `Parley <parley@localhost>`
   Check: integration
   - setup: an engine fixture: a real store and a bare repository in t.TempDir(), a workspace `api` with branch main, the default gate, and a helper that opens a change from a branch with given commits
   ```
   in internal/land/replay_test.go: main = A-B; the change's branch = A-c1-c2 (two authors, each touching its own file); run the attempt; assert it ended landed with attempts == 1 and onto_sha == B; assert git log main shows B <- c1' <- c2' with the authors, author dates and messages of c1 and c2 and committer 'Parley <parley@localhost>'; assert commits == [{change, version_sha: c1, landed_sha: c1'}, {change, version_sha: c2, landed_sha: c2'}] and landed_sha == c2'; assert the tree of c2' holds B's file and both of the change's files; with [land] committer_name 'Hub' and committer_email 'hub@example.org' the committer is 'Hub <hub@example.org>'
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN an attempt with strategy `rebase` replays a change whose first own commit has the target head as its parent, THE parleyd SHALL use the change's commits as they are, without creating any commit
   → the target moves to the version's head commit itself; every `commits` entry has `landed_sha` equal to `version_sha`
   Check: integration
   - setup: an engine fixture: a real store and a bare repository in t.TempDir(), a workspace `api` with branch main, the default gate, and a helper that opens a change from a branch with given commits
   ```
   in internal/land/replay_test.go: main = A-B; the change's branch = A-B-c1-c2; run the attempt; assert landed; assert main == c2 (the same id); assert commits == [{version_sha: c1, landed_sha: c1}, {version_sha: c2, landed_sha: c2}]; assert the committer of c2 is still the original one
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN an attempt with strategy `squash` replays a change, THE parleyd SHALL create one commit per change whose tree is the result of replaying the change's own commits onto the target head, whose author is the author of the version's head commit, and whose message is the change title, a blank line, the intent, a blank line and the trailers
   → the trailers are `Parley-Change: <slug>#<number>`, then `Parley-Session: <id>` only when the change has a session, then one `Co-authored-by: Name <email>` per distinct author of the change's own commits other than the head commit's author; `commits` has one entry for the change with `version_sha` the version's head
   Check: integration
   - setup: an engine fixture: a real store and a bare repository in t.TempDir(), a workspace `api` with branch main, the default gate, and a helper that opens a change from a branch with given commits

### REQ-5: Compare-and-swap with retry and atomic bookkeeping

**Rationale:** Without a queue, the compare-and-swap is the only thing that keeps two lands from overwriting each other, and the bookkeeping must never disagree with the ref (LAND-FR-014, LAND-FR-015, LAND-FR-021).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN the target head is no longer the head the replay was built on when the compare-and-swap is tried, THE parleyd SHALL read the new target head, replay the change again onto it and try the compare-and-swap again, counting the try in `attempts`
   → the attempt ends `landed` with `attempts` equal to the number of compare-and-swap tries (2 after one lost race) and `onto_sha` equal to the head the successful try was built on; its commits sit on top of the commits that moved the target
   Check: integration
   - setup: an engine fixture: a real store and a bare repository in t.TempDir(), a workspace `api` with branch main, the default gate, and a helper that opens a change from a branch with given commits
   ```
   in internal/land/engine_test.go with a test hook that runs between the replay and the compare-and-swap: on the first try the hook lands change A (a different file) on main; run the attempt for change B; assert B ended landed with attempts == 2 and onto_sha == A's landed_sha; assert git log main shows B's commit directly on top of A's; assert A's attempt has attempts == 1; repeat with the hook moving main by a direct ref update instead of a land: same assertions on attempts and parentage
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] IF the compare-and-swap has lost `[land].max_attempts` times (default 10) in one attempt, THEN THE parleyd SHALL end the attempt `failed` with `error` `contention`
   → the attempt is final with `status` `failed`, `error` `contention` and `attempts` equal to the limit; the HTTP answer is 503 with `error_type` `land_failed` and the land attempt in `error.details`; none of the attempt's commits is in the target; the change stays `open` and can be landed by a new call
   Check: integration
   - setup: an engine fixture: a real store and a bare repository in t.TempDir(), a workspace `api` with branch main, the default gate, and a helper that opens a change from a branch with given commits
   ```
   in internal/land/engine_test.go: [land].max_attempts = 3; the test hook moves main with an unrelated commit before every compare-and-swap; run the attempt; assert status == 'failed' and error == 'contention' and attempts == 3 and landed_sha == null; assert main holds only the hook's commits; assert the change reads open; assert one land_fail event with status 'failed' and reason 'contention'; with the default configuration assert the loop stops after 10 tries
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN the compare-and-swap of the target succeeds, THE parleyd SHALL record, as one atomic step with the ref move, each landed change's transition to `landed`, the mapping of each landed commit to its change, the attempt's final status and one `parley.change.land` event per landed change

### REQ-6: Stack landing

**Rationale:** A stack is reviewed bottom up but is often ready as a whole; landing it in one move keeps the target from ever holding half of it (LAND-FR-016).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN a land request with `stack: true` passes the entry checks and the preconditions, THE parleyd SHALL cover the named change and every unlanded change below it in one attempt, replay all of them bottom first onto the target head and move the target once, to the top
   → `changes` lists the covered changes bottom first; the target moves exactly once; every covered change is `landed` by the same attempt and `landed.sha` is the new target head; one `parley.change.land` event is written per landed change and one `parley.git.push`; with `squash` each change becomes one commit, in order
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub test fixture: a real store in t.TempDir(), a bare repository created with git init whose branch main holds one commit, a ready workspace `api` owned by user `owner`, and the land routes mounted on the real server pipeline with stub authentication
   ```
   in internal/land/stack_test.go: changes 1 <- 2 <- 3 (depends_on chain) on main, main moved by one unrelated commit M; r = land(3, {stack: true}); assert r.status == 200; a = r.json; assert a.changes == [1, 2, 3] and a.attempts == 1; assert git log main shows M followed by the commits of 1, then 2, then 3; assert a.commits lists them in that order with their change numbers; assert changes 1, 2 and 3 each read landed with landed.land_id == a.id and landed.sha == a.landed_sha; assert three parley.change.land events (resource_id '1', '2', '3') and exactly one parley.git.push via land; with land.strategy squash assert exactly three new commits on main, one per change in order, and a.commits has three entries
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] WHEN a stack land finds a change below that is already `landed`, THE parleyd SHALL leave that change out of the attempt
   → `changes` holds only the unlanded changes; the landed change keeps its `landed` object and gets no second event
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub test fixture: a real store in t.TempDir(), a bare repository created with git init whose branch main holds one commit, a ready workspace `api` owned by user `owner`, and the land routes mounted on the real server pipeline with stub authentication
   ```
   in internal/land/stack_test.go: changes 1 <- 2 <- 3; change 1 is landed by its own call and the dependants still record the chain; r = land(3, {stack: true}); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.changes == [2, 3]; assert change 1's landed.land_id is still the first attempt's and only one parley.change.land event exists for it

1. [REQ-6.3] IF a change below the named change that a stack land would cover is `draft` or `abandoned`, or is covered by a `running` land attempt, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the stack land before creating an attempt
   → HTTP 409 with `error_type` `change_not_open` for a `draft` or `abandoned` change below, or `land_in_progress` with the running land attempt in `error.details`; no land attempt is created and the target does not move

   ```

   → the attempt is final with `status` `conflict` and `conflict.change` naming the change, or `status` `blocked` and `blocked.change` naming it; the target does not move and every covered change stays `open`; one `parley.change.land_fail` event is written, on the named change

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An agent lands a change from the command line

1. **agent** pushes a branch with two commits to a task fork with a git client and opens a change into the parent's main
2. **developer** pushes an unrelated commit to main, so that the change no longer sits on the target head
3. **agent** runs `parley change land <slug> <number> --wait`
4. **parley CLI** sends POST /workspaces/<slug>/changes/<number>/land and, on a 202, polls GET /workspaces/<slug>/lands/<id>
5. **parleyd** checks scope, access and the preconditions, creates the land attempt and asks the default policy gate, which answers ready
6. **parleyd** replays the two commits onto the target head, moves main by compare-and-swap and records the landed change, the commit mapping, the final attempt and the events in one step
7. **parleyd** deletes the source branch in the fork and answers the land attempt with status landed
8. **parley CLI** prints the land attempt and exits 0
9. **git client** fetches main from the parent workspace and receives the developer's commit followed by the two landed commits

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd started in-process on a loopback listener with its real store and repository storage, the git smart HTTP server and push rules, the change routes of package 22, the land routes, engine and worker pool, the event log, the parley CLI binary's root command, the git binary as client and on the server

**Setup:**

- a hub started by the run function of package 01 with a temporary data directory
- a workspace `api` cloned from a local bare origin, owned by `owner`
- a task fork of `api` created by `owner` and a change opened from its branch `feat`

**End state:**

- the CLI exited 0 and its stdout is a land attempt with status landed, attempts 1 and two commits entries
- `git fetch` of main shows the developer's commit followed by two commits whose authors are the agent's and whose committer is Parley <parley@localhost>
- GET of the change reads state landed with landed.land_id equal to the attempt's id
- the fork no longer has the branch feat
- GET /events/log holds one parley.change.land event and one parley.git.push event with via land for main
- the origin repository's main has not moved

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/land_test.go: hub = startHub(t); ws = createWorkspace('api', origin); fork = createFork(ws); git push fork feat (2 commits); n = openChange(fork, 'feat'); git push ws main (1 unrelated commit, as owner); out, code = parley('change', 'land', 'api', n, '--wait'); assert code == 0; a = json(out); assert a.status == 'landed' and len(a.commits) == 2; git fetch ws main; assert log == [M, c1', c2'] and committer(c2') == 'Parley <parley@localhost>'; assert getChange(n).state == 'landed' and getChange(n).landed.land_id == a.id; assert !refExists(fork, 'feat'); assert events('parley.change.land') == 1 and events('parley.git.push', via='land') == 1; assert rev(origin, 'main') == originHeadBefore
```

### PATH-2: Two agents land on one target at the same moment

1. **agent** two agents each open a change into main from their own fork; the changes touch different files
2. **agent** both send POST /workspaces/<slug>/changes/<number>/land at the same moment
3. **parleyd** runs both land attempts concurrently on the worker pool, each replaying onto the head it read
4. **parleyd** moves main for the attempt whose compare-and-swap comes first; the other attempt sees the target moved, replays onto the new head and moves main again
5. **parleyd** answers both calls 200 with a landed attempt
6. **git client** fetches main and finds both changes' commits in one linear history

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd started in-process with its real store and repository storage, the land routes, engine and worker pool, the change routes of package 22, the git binary

**Setup:**

- a hub with a workspace `api` and 8 forks, each with one open change into main that adds its own file
- no test hook installed in the engine

**End state:**

- all 8 land calls, started together, answered 200 with status landed; no call was repeated
- main has a linear history that holds all 8 files
- every attempt has attempts between 1 and 8, and the attempts of all sum to at least 8
- every change reads state landed and each landed commit resolves to its change through the by-commit lookup
- the event log holds 8 parley.change.land events and 8 parley.git.push events with via land, whose before and after values chain from the old head to the new one

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/land_test.go: start 8 goroutines, each POST …/changes/<n>/land; wait; assert every status == 200 and body.status == 'landed'; git clone ws; assert the 8 files exist and `git rev-list --merges main` is empty; pushes = events('parley.git.push', via='land') ordered by seq; assert pushes[0].before == oldHead and pushes[i].before == pushes[i-1].after and pushes[7].after == rev('main')
```

### PATH-3: A land that conflicts comes back as a report and changes nothing

1. **agent** two agents each open a change into main that edits the same line of the same file
2. **agent** the first agent sends POST …/land for its change
3. **parleyd** lands the first change and answers 200
4. **agent** the second agent sends POST …/land for its change
5. **parleyd** replays the second change onto the new head, finds that its commit does not apply and builds the conflict report naming the file and the first change
6. **parleyd** ends the attempt conflict, leaves main where it is, marks the change mergeable conflict, writes parley.change.land_fail and answers 409 land_conflict with the attempt in details
7. **developer** reads GET /workspaces/<slug>/lands/<id> and GET /workspaces/<slug>/changes/<number>/lands and sees the same attempt

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd started in-process with its real store and repository storage, the land routes and engine, the change routes of packages 22 and 23, the event log, the git binary

**Setup:**

- a hub with a workspace `api` whose main holds f.txt
- two forks, each with an open change editing line 3 of f.txt differently

**End state:**

- the second land answered 409 with error_type land_conflict
- the attempt in error.details has status conflict and a report whose files is one entry for f.txt with kind content and landed_by naming the first change, and whose landed_changes names the first change with its landed_sha
- main still equals the first change's landed_sha
- the second change reads state open and mergeable conflict
- GET …/lands/<id> returns the same attempt, and the change's land list holds it
- the event log holds one parley.change.land_fail event for the second change with status conflict

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/land_test.go: r1 = land(c1); assert r1.status == 200; head = rev('main'); r2 = land(c2); assert r2.status == 409 and r2.error.error_type == 'land_conflict'; k = r2.error.details.conflict; assert k.files[0].path == 'f.txt' and k.files[0].kind == 'content' and k.files[0].landed_by == [c1]; assert k.landed_changes[0].number == c1 and k.landed_changes[0].landed_sha == head; assert rev('main') == head; assert getChange(c2).state == 'open' and getChange(c2).mergeable == 'conflict'; assert get('/lands/' + r2.error.details.id) == r2.error.details; assert events('parley.change.land_fail', resource_id=c2) == 1
```

### PATH-4: A land in flight during a restart finishes afterwards

1. **agent** sends POST …/land?wait=0 for an open change and receives 202 with a running attempt
2. **operator** stops parleyd before a worker has finished the attempt
3. **operator** starts parleyd again on the same data directory
4. **parleyd** completes any journalled move whose ref already holds the new head, then finds the running attempt and runs it again from the preconditions
5. **parleyd** replays, moves main and records the land in one step
6. **agent** polls GET /workspaces/<slug>/lands/<id> and reads status landed

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd started in-process twice on one data directory, the store and its schema migration, the land engine, journal, worker pool and start-up recovery, the change routes of package 22, the git binary

**Setup:**

- a hub with a workspace `api` and one open change
- [land].workers set so that the first hub does not start the attempt before it is stopped (the pool is paused by the test option of the composition in internal/hub/land.go)

**End state:**

- after the second start the attempt with the id the 202 returned reads status landed
- main holds the change's commits exactly once
- the change reads state landed with landed.land_id equal to that id
- the event log holds exactly one parley.change.land event for the change
- no land attempt of the workspace is left running

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/land_test.go: hub1 = startHub(t, dir, pausedLandPool); a = post('/workspaces/api/changes/1/land?wait=0'); assert a.status == 202; hub1.stop(); hub2 = startHub(t, dir); eventually(get('/workspaces/api/lands/' + a.id).status == 'landed'); assert count(commits of the change in main) == 1; assert getChange(1).landed.land_id == a.id; assert events('parley.change.land') == 1; assert list('/workspaces/api/lands?status=running').items == []
```

- 5.3 Fail loading with an error that names the key (land.max_attempts, land.workers, land.timeout, land.committer_name, land.committer_email) for max_attempts or workers below 1, a timeout that is not a positive duration, and an empty committer name or email, so that parleyd exits non-zero before listening
- 5.4 Add the pool in internal/land/pool.go: at most `workers` attempts are computed at once; a submitted attempt that finds no free worker waits and stays running; waiting attempts are started in no promised order and submission never fails because the pool is full
- 5.5 Give every attempt a deadline of `timeout` counted from its creation (or from its re-queue at start); when it passes, cancel the attempt's context so a running git command is killed, and finish the attempt failed with error timeout, also when it never got a worker
- 5.6 Make sure an attempt that timed out cannot move the target afterwards: the engine checks its context immediately before the compare-and-swap and the finish operation refuses a second final status
- 5.7 Let waiters subscribe to an attempt's end, so that the land route can wait for a final status without polling the store
- 5.8 Start the pool from the composition in internal/hub/land.go with the loaded [land] options and stop it at shutdown without finishing running attempts (they stay running for recovery)

### 6. Serve the land route: who may land, what the request may carry, and the answer (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-2.1, REQ-5.5, REQ-8.4

**Steps:**

- 6.1 Add the entry-check, attempt-creation, concurrency and wait behaviours to internal/land/routes_test.go, with the routes mounted on the real pipeline of package 02 and a clock the test controls, and confirm they fail
- 6.2 Register POST /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/land with scope changes:write, workspace need read and the create-route declaration for Idempotency-Key
- 6.3 In internal/land/authz.go admit the caller whose level on the target workspace is owner or admin, or whose user is the change's author while the setting land.by_author is true; answer every other member 403 forbidden; answer 409 workspace_archived for an archived target after that check
- 6.4 For a caller whose token is bound to a task fork of the target, answer 403 token_bound when the change's source workspace is not that fork, when a stack land would cover a change with another source, on GET …/changes/:number/lands for such a change, on GET …/lands/:id for an attempt none of whose changes comes from the fork, and on GET …/lands; an unknown change or id keeps its 404
- 6.5 Validate the body and query: expected_version an integer of at least 1, stack a boolean, override an object with a non-empty string reason, session_id a string, wait a whole number from 0 to 60 with default 30; answer 400 invalid_request otherwise
- 6.6 Declare the session interface of internal/land with two operations, check and record, which package 49 installs from the linking check and the recording operation of internal/session; check a given session_id through it (same user or admin token; the session's workspace is the target, a fork of it or its parent) and answer 400 unknown_session on failure; with no implementation installed every session id fails the rule
- 6.7 Create the running attempt with trigger manual, the strategy read once from land.strategy, requested_by from the caller, the session and the current version of the change, record a land link for the session through the session interface in the same transaction, then submit it to the pool; expose the same start as a function that takes the change, the trigger, the requested_by to store and the actor of the attempt's events, checks the preconditions and asks no request guard, for package 29's automatic landing
- 6.8 Wait for the attempt's end for up to `wait` seconds; answer 200 with the attempt when it is landed and 202 with the running attempt when the wait runs out; a client that disconnects does not cancel the attempt
- 6.9 Hold no lock across an attempt: two attempts for different changes on one target run at the same time and meet only in the compare-and-swap

### 8. End an attempt as conflict, blocked or failed and tell the caller (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4.5, REQ-3, REQ-8.3, REQ-8.5

**Steps:**

- 8.1 Add the conflict, gate and answer behaviours to internal/land/routes_test.go, internal/land/gate_test.go and internal/land/engine_test.go and confirm they fail
- 8.2 When a commit does not apply, fill the ConflictReport of internal/gitrepo in internal/land/conflict.go: target_sha (the head replayed onto), head_sha (the version's head), base_sha (the version's base), commit_sha (the first commit that did not apply), the classified files, and change null for a single-change attempt
- 8.3 Add the attribution as one exported function of internal/land/conflict.go that takes a report and fills landed_changes and each file's landed_by from the landed-commit mapping: the changes whose landed commits lie between base_sha and target_sha and touch a conflicted path, each as {number, title, landed_sha, session_id}; it leaves both empty when none is found, when base_sha is not an ancestor of target_sha or when the mapping cannot be read; package 26 calls the same function for the other producers of a report
- 8.4 Finish the attempt conflict with the report, leave the target untouched, and record mergeable conflict with the same report on the change through package 23's mergeability recorder
- 8.5 When the gate answers pending or blocked for a change, finish the attempt blocked with blocked {change, status, requirements} of the first such change, bottom first, without replaying
- 8.6 Ask the gate once per change per attempt and not again on a compare-and-swap retry; for an answer that is not ready on a request with override, ask the override rule and treat a passed answer as ready; record override {reason} on the attempt and in the parley.change.land metadata only when the rule let at least one change pass
- 8.7 Write one parley.change.land_fail event in the transaction that finishes an attempt as conflict, blocked or failed: resource the change that stopped it (else the top change), actor the caller, the request's session, metadata land_id, status, reason and, for a conflict, files; reason is conflict, the gate's reason or policy, or the error value
- 8.8 Answer a final attempt on the land route as 409 land_conflict, 409 policy_blocked or 503 land_failed, each with the attempt as error.details, through the error value of package 02

### 9. Land with the squash strategy and land a whole stack (implement)

- 9.3 Record one commits entry per squashed change with version_sha the version's head

- 9.5 Apply the open check and the running-attempt check to every covered change before the attempt is created: 409 change_not_open for a draft or abandoned change below, 409 land_in_progress with the running attempt for one that is being landed; a single-change land of a change covered by a running stack attempt gets land_in_progress too

### 10. Do the follow-up work of a land and offer guards, hooks and observers (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7

**Steps:**

- 10.1 Add the follow-up behaviours to internal/land/after_test.go and internal/land/hooks_test.go and confirm they fail
- 10.2 Add four registration points in internal/land/hooks.go: request guards (asked with the caller, the workspace, the changes the attempt would cover and the request's override; answer allow or a refusal with HTTP status, error_type and optional path), target guards (asked with workspace, target branch, old head and new head; answer allow, refuse with a reason, or origin rejected with a message, or return an error instead of an answer), after-landing hooks (called with the landed attempt, the target workspace, the update of the target branch as ref, before and after, the attempt's session id and, per landed change, its number, source workspace and branch and landed commit) and final observers (called with the final attempt, its result, attempts and duration)
- 10.3 Ask the request guards in the land route after the entry checks and the body validation and before the preconditions; return the first refusal as the route's answer and create no attempt; the start function for trigger auto_land asks none
- 10.4 Ask the guards after the replay and before the first compare-and-swap: a refusal finishes the attempt blocked with blocked {change, status blocked, requirements empty} and the guard's reason as the land_fail reason; an origin rejection finishes it failed with error origin_rejected; a guard error finishes it failed with error internal and never allows; the target does not move in any of the three cases
- 10.5 After the atomic step of a landed attempt, also a no-op one, delete each landed change's source branch when land.delete_source is true, by compare-and-swap against the landed version's head and only when no other draft or open change has that branch as source
- 10.6 Then ask package 23's scheduler for a mergeability check of every other draft or open change on the target branch, and call each after-landing hook once; this package registers none itself: package 24 registers its landing entry point, package 16 its fork activity hook and package 37 its rebuild trigger
- 10.7 Run every follow-up step independently: recover from a panic, log a failure, and change neither the attempt nor the HTTP answer nor the remaining steps
- 10.8 Report every attempt that reaches a final status once to every final observer, with the time from its creation to its end
- 10.9 Make no call to origin or to a forge anywhere in the land
